priorStories.headline: Democrats win control of the U.S. Senate
priorStories.body:
CBS News projected that Democrats had secured enough Republican-held seats to overturn the GOP’s 53-47 majority and take control of the Senate.

Projected Democratic pickups included Texas, North Carolina, South Carolina, Ohio, Kansas and Iowa. Democrats also retained seats in Georgia and New Hampshire. The final size of their majority remained undetermined.

priorStories.headline: First Black and Native American women elected governors
priorStories.body:
Georgia voters elected Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms, making her the first Black woman elected governor of any U.S. state and Georgia’s first governor of color.

New Mexico elected Democrat Deb Haaland, a citizen of the Laguna Pueblo, as the first Native American woman to serve as a U.S. governor.

candidates.summary: The Associated Press called control of the U.S. House for Democrats at 1:26 a.m. Eastern, giving the party majorities in both chambers of Congress. AP later reported Democrats had won well beyond the 218 House seats required for control, ending two years of unified Republican control when the new Congress convenes in January.
candidates.title: Democrats win control of the U.S. House

candidates.summary: Michigan elected Democrat Abdul El-Sayed as the first Muslim U.S. senator. Other Senate results reported by the Associated Press included Peggy Flanagan of Minnesota becoming the first Native American woman elected to the chamber and Chris Pappas of New Hampshire becoming its first openly gay male member. Illinois elected Julia Stratton, meaning three Black women will serve simultaneously in the Senate for the first time.
candidates.title: U.S. Senate elections produce several representation firsts

candidates.summary: Israel’s Central Elections Committee certified the results of the October 27 general election after reviewing complaints and finding no irregularities that compromised the result. The Netanyahu-aligned bloc received 53 Knesset seats, Gadi Eisenkot’s opposition bloc 48 and Arab-led parties 19, leaving no bloc with the 61 seats needed to govern. President Isaac Herzog began consultations before assigning a candidate to try to form a coalition.
candidates.title: Israel certifies inconclusive election results

candidates.summary: The Associated Press reported, citing people familiar with his plans, that House Speaker Mike Johnson would not seek election as House Republican leader after Democrats won control of the chamber. Republicans will hold internal leadership elections before the new Congress convenes in January.
candidates.title: Mike Johnson reported to be leaving House Republican leadership

candidates.summary: Yemen’s internationally recognized government said its forces had advanced farther into the al-Dahida mountain range in eastern al-Jawf province after claiming control of the strategic heights a day earlier. The military said troops supported by aircraft and drones seized Houthi fortifications, weapons and equipment. The account had not been independently verified in the cited report.
candidates.title: Yemeni government forces claim further advance in al-Jawf

candidates.summary: U.S. stocks rallied following the midterm elections, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average rising by more than 1,000 points during Wednesday trading. Shares of Trump Media & Technology Group fell 13.7 percent, while major U.S. defense contractors also declined amid expectations that Democratic control of Congress could affect administration policy.
candidates.title: Dow rises more than 1,000 points after U.S. midterms
